headline: Apple updates App Store rules to ban AI 'nudify' apps
summary: Apple tightened App Store rules against AI apps that generate nonconsensual intimate images, often called 'nudify' apps, following criticism over X and Grok. One report frames the policy narrowly as targeting nonconsensual deepfake generators, while another frames it as a broader crackdown on apps that fail to moderate offensive content.

claims.statement: Apple updated or tightened its App Store rules to ban AI apps that generate nonconsensual intimate ('nudify') images.

sources.quote: Apple’s updated App Store rules go after ‘nudify’ AI apps
Apple has tightened the App Store's rules against AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery.
Apple updates guidelines to ban nudify apps masquerading as regular apps to pass review

claims.statement: The rule change follows criticism of Apple after X users used Grok to make nonconsensual sexualized deepfakes, including of minors.

sources.quote: The rule changes follow significant criticism toward Apple after X users used Grok earlier this year to make nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes, including minors.

claims.statement: TechCrunch describes the policy as banning AI apps generally that fail to moderate offensive content, and apps that disguise themselves to pass App Store review.

sources.quote: Apple said that it will ban AI apps that don't moderate offensive content.

discrepancies.explanation: TechCrunch's lede frames the policy as a broader ban on apps that fail to moderate offensive content, while the Verge and Engadget describe it specifically as targeting nonconsensual intimate-image apps.

quotes.quote: Apple said that it will ban AI apps that don't moderate offensive content.
Apple has tightened the App Store's rules against AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery.
